title: Humanity Restored in Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Humanity restored in Christ means that Jesus redeems fallen people and renews them toward God’s image, purpose, holiness, and eternal life. Restoration is not self-improvement, but God making sinners new through Christ.
summary: Humanity restored in Christ means that Jesus redeems fallen people and renews them toward God’s image, purpose, holiness, and eternal life. Restoration is not self-improvement, but God making sinners new through Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the true image of God, the last Adam, and the Savior who restores fallen humanity. In Him, believers are forgiven, renewed, conformed to His image, and destined for glory.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin has ruined humanity, but it has not outrun God’s redemptive purpose. Christ came to restore what was broken by the fall and bring His people back to God.

Jesus is the true man and last Adam. Where Adam brought sin and death, Christ brings righteousness and life. Those united to Him are being renewed after His image.

This restoration begins now and will be completed in glory. Believers are new creations, yet still await the full redemption of body, soul, relationships, and creation. God’s work is already real but not yet finished.

Final restoration is not merely personal improvement. God will dwell with His people, wipe away tears, defeat death, and make all things new through Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often settle for a small hope: coping better, sinning less, feeling better, or rebuilding a damaged life. Those may be gifts, but Christ promises something greater—true restoration to God’s purpose.

This doctrine speaks hope to the fallen, disabled, ashamed, addicted, wounded, and weary. In Christ, brokenness is not the final word. God is restoring His people toward glory.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Set your hope on Christ’s restoring work, not on self-made improvement. Yield to His renewing grace now through repentance, faith, Scripture, obedience, and fellowship. When your growth feels slow, remember that the Savior who began restoration will complete it in glory.
